known.title: Preserve keyboard focus across successive live redraws
Remove Git command text from assignment refusals

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Calling focus() synchronously triggers the new control's focusin handler, which records its replacement node in last; the following last = null immediately erases that record. A second live redraw therefore removes the focused username field without restoring focus. On an active story whose parts change while a manager types, keyboard input stops reaching the field. Keep the replacement focus record so restoration works on every redraw. Both drawer and full-page controls use this path; item.js:379–383 redraws them when their rows change.
findings.title: Preserve keyboard focus across successive live redraws

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. The filter rejects forge commands and flags but accepts Git command text. Every assignment fetches first (task.py:234 and :136); an ordinary network or authentication failure is converted by cli.py:158–161 into a refusal beginning "git fetch failed: ...". This function returns that technical text directly to the board, without a recovery action. Handle this transport failure with a plain-language reason and next step while retaining the detailed command error in the terminal.
findings.title: Remove Git command text from assignment refusals

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. The promised teammate-board proof ends with a fresh CLI JSON derivation; it never opens a teammate's live board before the assignment or verifies its refresh afterward. A board that stops noticing fetched remote story-branch changes would still pass this test. The existing server test at tests/test_board_server.py:189–216 changes the default branch instead, so it does not cover this publication path. Keep a teammate board running and assert that its displayed owner changes after it receives the assignment.
